title: RB-1 — Report Blocks Cutover Delivery
summary: replace singular document report front matter with one validated block-level report host across source, projections, runtime, and dependent services
content_html:
RB-1 — Report Blocks Cutover Delivery

Status And Purpose

RB-1 is in progress at the RB-1.2 review gate. It delivers the complete Report Blocks source-contract cutover: every report-host document moves from viewer_report* front matter to one validated block in its Markdown body, every consumer reads one normalized descriptor, and the browser mounts the report at that exact authored position.

RB-1.2 is complete: builders, services, workflows, Manage/public runtime, all 13 authoritative hosts, affected generated products, and the two public Analysis projections use the normalized report descriptor and exact authored host. No compatibility reader remains. Stop here for review before RB-1.3 verification and durable ownership transfer.

The feature contract is settled. RB-1.0 identifies the exact implementation seams and migration footprint; it does not reopen the rejected multiple-instance, parameter, registry, plugin, or capability models already owned by Report Blocks.

Complete Outcome

  • A document contains zero or one report block. Multiple blocks and a mixture of report front matter plus a report block fail source validation.
  • One code-owned parser recognizes the fixed block grammar only in accepted Markdown contexts and returns one normalized document-level descriptor.
  • The descriptor carries registered report identity and the existing closed assignment context: access intent, scope, preset, and sub-scope where applicable.
  • The docs builder emits one inert report host at the block's exact content position plus one normalized payload descriptor. It no longer appends an independently created report root after the document.
  • Public and Manage report composition resolve the descriptor through their existing separate metadata and executable loader allowlists, then mount into that exact generated host.
  • The immutable document doc_id remains the report-host identity.
  • Sub-scope lifecycle, location, publication, deletion, transfer, and other exact-host consumers use the same normalized source owner as the builder rather than reading private front-matter fields or independently scanning Markdown.
  • Every current repository or external-local report-host source is converted in one bounded migration, every affected projection is rebuilt, and active product code contains no compatibility reader or precedence rule for the retired fields.
  • Existing reports retain their report id, access, scope, preset, sub-scope, data authority, public/local composition, route state, and behavior apart from their authored placement.

Current Owners To Inspect

RB-1.0 starts from these ownership seams and narrows the exact changed set before implementation:

  • Docs source parsing, DocRecord, content-token resolution, Markdown rendering, Manage/public metadata projection, and report metadata registry validation;
  • public and Manage document-extras entrypoints, report controllers, executable loader allowlists, and report lifecycle cleanup;
  • sub-scope source creation and host discovery, document-location composition and projection, publish eligibility, deletion follow-through, document transfer, and any other exact report-host readers;
  • complete-source Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export workflows that could otherwise treat a report block as ordinary transferable prose;
  • every current report-host source across repository and configured external-local scopes, including lifecycle-created docs_subscope hosts;
  • focused builder, service, public-boundary, report-module, sub-scope lifecycle, and route smokes; and
  • Reports, Report Capability and Composition, and Sub-Scope Customisation Architecture as likely durable documentation owners.

This is an inspection route, not a frozen file inventory. RB-1.0 must report exact files, reused seams, estimated production/test footprint, and any workflow whose existing report-host behavior needs an explicit retain, omit, or reject decision.

Delivery Steps

RB-1.0 — Confirm Contract And Cutover Fit

  • [x] Inventory every active viewer_report* source field, parser, payload writer, browser reader, service reader, source writer, fixture, test, report host, and generated projection.
  • [x] Fix one exact block syntax, allowed attribute names and values, whitespace and escaping rules, placement rule, ignored Markdown contexts, and errors for malformed, duplicate, mixed-contract, or unknown declarations.
  • [x] Freeze the normalized in-process descriptor, generated payload shape, inert host markup, public/Manage projection behavior, and exact browser mount/unmount contract.
  • [x] Confirm how local-only blocks, public-intended but unpromoted reports, and promoted public reports appear in Manage and public document projections without weakening the existing module/data boundary.
  • [x] Confirm the exact docs_subscope creation, discovery, recorded-host validation, location, publication, deletion, and transfer changes required to preserve current child routes and lifecycle ownership.
  • [x] Inspect Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export flows and decide explicitly whether a report block is retained, omitted, rejected, or rendered inert in each existing workflow.
  • [x] Inventory all current report-host documents and affected scopes, then define the direct source migration and rebuild matrix.
  • [x] Restate the proposed production files, focused tests, generated products, rough diff size, risks, and rollback boundary before implementation.

Checkpoint: one concise RB-1.0 sanity record confirms the grammar, normalized descriptor, projection and mount flow, source-workflow decisions, exact host migration, implementation footprint, focused evidence, and any unresolved implementation decision. Stop before RB-1.1 implementation approval.

RB-1.0 sanity record

Source grammar. One report block uses this exact source form:

:::report
id: docs_index_table
access: local
scope: analysis
preset: scope_documents_admin
:::

The opener is exactly :::report and the closer is exactly ::: at column one, each on its own line with no trailing content. The block must be separated from surrounding Markdown by at least one blank line unless it begins or ends the body. Interior lines use exactly key: value; blank lines, indentation, inline attributes, quoting, escaping, multiline values, and duplicate keys are invalid. id and access are required. Optional keys are scope, preset, and sub_scope; the emitter uses that canonical order, while the parser does not make key order semantic. Identifier values use lowercase ASCII letters, digits, _, and -, beginning with a letter or digit. access is exactly local or public. There are no aliases such as report, subscope, or manage.

The parser ignores apparent declarations inside backtick or tilde fenced code, indented code, inline code, HTML comments, and raw <pre> or <code> regions. A declaration-like :::report line outside those contexts is structural and must either form one valid block or fail. Two valid blocks, an unclosed block, malformed interior syntax, unknown keys or values, an unknown report id, a report block in a sub-scope child document, or any mixture with one of the five retired front-matter keys fails with the source path, line, and exact source range. The five retired keys fail even when blank.

The source registry remains docs-viewer/config/reports/reports.json; no new registry is introduced. Report ids and presets validate against it. scope validates against configured scopes and is accepted only by docs_index_table, docs_broken_links, and semantic_tokens. preset is accepted only by docs_index_table and must name one of that registry entry's presets. sub_scope is required only by docs_subscope, is forbidden for other reports, and must name one configured child collection of the host document's own scope. All other current reports accept only id and access.

Normalized owner and projection. The new shared Python owner returns one immutable descriptor with id, resolved access, optional scope, preset, and sub_scope, plus exact source offsets and line numbers used only in process. The JSON projection is one fixed-shape report object with those five keys; absent optional values are null, and source ranges are never projected. A non-report document has no report key.

Manage by-ID payloads retain every valid local or public descriptor. Public by-ID payloads emit a descriptor only when access is public. The builder replaces the source range with <section class="docsViewerReport" data-docs-viewer-report-host aria-label="Document report"></section> for each projection that carries the descriptor; it removes a local-only block from public content. Tree, Recent, search, manifests, and semantic-token indexes do not receive report metadata.

The existing Manage and public document-extras entrypoints read payload.report, require exactly one generated host inside the current document content, and pass that host to the existing separate registry and executable-loader allowlists. They never create or append a second root. A public-intended but unpromoted report keeps its descriptor and host and receives the existing contained unavailable state; a local-only report has neither in public output; promoted docs_subscope continues to mount through the public registry and loader. Navigation replaces the document content and therefore removes the exact host; the existing docs_subscope mutation observer publishes its unmount event, and stale asynchronous work must not mutate a host that is no longer contained by the current document root. No controller, stylesheet, loader graph, data authority, route, or report-module contract changes.

Sub-scope lifecycle. Parent-host discovery in the parent builder, canonical document URLs, document-location source and public projections, Publish placement, lifecycle claimant checks, recorded-host deletion validation, and transfer route rewriting all consume the shared descriptor. New sub-scope creation writes the canonical block immediately after the generated H1. Lifecycle deletion still requires the recorded immutable report_host_doc_id, exact source revision, docs_subscope, local access, the exact configured child id, and one claimant. The existing analysis/works and dotlineform/projects lifecycle source-revision receipts change once during migration; their ids, tool ownership, collection configuration, URLs, and deletion rules do not.

Complete-source workflow decisions. The direct Source editor retains report blocks and validates the complete candidate before write. Generic Copy/Document Transfer rejects a selected report-host document because Report Blocks authorizes no host-transfer contract; ordinary child copying is unchanged, and transfer route rewriting still resolves the source collection's parent host through the shared descriptor. Ordinary Import rejects any incoming report block and rejects replacement of an existing report-host document, so imported prose cannot acquire or erase report configuration. The current returned document-content Review flow may export report-host prose but cannot apply a replacement to that exact host; the inactive document-full-source idea receives no new support. document-tree omits report configuration, while rendered document-content packages explicitly omit the empty generated host. Static HTML export retains the generated host at its exact content position as inert markup; it exports no report descriptor, registry, loader, service, or report JavaScript. Metadata-only edits, Publishability changes, and exact Source edits retain and revalidate the existing block.

Current host and projection inventory. Thirteen authoritative hosts exist now:

Scope Host documents Access/context
analysis d-20260624-213316-478639 Concepts; d-20260807-082735-54d9d5 Works public docs_subscope; tags and works
studio d-20260423-165116-e7f7e9 Broken Links; d-20260507-123607-fd7cff Analysis Documents; d-20260513-105343-6de36b Reports; d-20260514-123140-83239c Source Config Report; d-20260726-181045-a7c2e1 Semantic Tokens Report; d-20260731-185207-2dbb6f Sub-Scope Default Report six local reports; Analysis Documents carries scope=analysis and preset=scope_documents_admin; Semantic Tokens carries scope=analysis; the default host carries sub_scope=default
dotlineform external-local d-20260801-073826-8865a8 Projects; d-20260805-155400-4c341f Project State; d-20260807-163356-b376d7 Uncataloged Files; d-20260807-175649-62020b Missing Source Files; d-20260810-150346-bc7cdc Works five local reports; Projects carries sub_scope=projects

The direct migration removes the five fields and appends one canonical block at the end of each current body, preserving the current append-after-prose presentation. It preserves doc_id, title, hierarchy, publishability, added_date, and last_updated; the migration is structural and must not reorder Recently Edited. The affected generated set is 13 Manage/working by-ID payloads plus the two public Analysis by-ID payloads. Index, Recent, search, location, manifest, and semantic-token outputs are rebuilt or checked but should remain semantically unchanged. The migration updates the two lifecycle source-revision receipts in docs-viewer/config/scopes/docs_scopes.json from the exact migrated source bytes.

Implementation footprint. RB-1.1 proposes one new pure owner, docs-viewer/services/docs_report_source.py, and docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_report_source.py; it should add roughly 180–240 production lines and 220–300 focused test lines without product integration. RB-1.2 proposes changes to docs_source_model.py; docs_builder/source.py, payloads.py, and sub_scope.py; docs_management_source_service.py, docs_import_document.py, docs_document_location.py, docs_document_location_projection.py, docs_publish_gate.py, docs_sub_scope_lifecycle.py, and docs_document_transfer.py; package rendered_content.py; the four Manage/public report entry/controller modules; and the shared docs-subscope-report.js retired-field message. No CSS, route, report registry, report implementation, controller, schema service, or general Markdown extension is proposed. That product slice is estimated at another 260–380 production lines changed and 350–550 focused test/fixture lines across builder/public payload, source editor, Import, package/static export, sub-scope lifecycle/location/Publish/transfer, report runtime, and current Studio Tag fixtures.

Focused evidence will use the new pure parser test; test_build_docs_payloads.py, test_build_docs_public_payloads.py, test_build_docs_subscopes.py, test_build_document_locations.py, test_docs_publish_gate.py, test_docs_scope_lifecycle.py, test_docs_management_subscope_delete.py, the three document-transfer test owners, test_docs_import_document.py, test_docs_management_source_service.py, test_docs_document_package_service.py, and test_docs_static_html_export.py; affected current fixtures and report-contract tests; and docs_viewer_subscope_report_modules.py, sub-scope create/delete workflow smokes, route navigation, and service-manage smoke. Changed Python and JavaScript receive focused lint. Studio, Analysis, and external-local dotlineform docs/search are rebuilt with the configured Projects base; Analysis then uses the existing scope-wide Publish boundary for its two public host payloads and document-location verification. Final evidence includes a retired-contract scan and git diff --check; the maintained docs-viewer-smoke profile is reserved for RB-1.3 boundary verification.

Risks and rollback. The principal risks are a scanner accepting examples as declarations, public output leaking local intent, a second appended browser root, stale lifecycle source revisions, generic Import/Transfer activating a copied block, and partial migration across the external-local source boundary. The pure parser gate isolates grammar risk before product integration. RB-1.2 is one all-or-nothing cutover: capture hashes and temporary preimages for the five external-local hosts, edit only the 13 inventoried sources, update both lifecycle receipts from final bytes, rebuild all three scopes, publish Analysis through the existing gate, and run the complete retired-field assertion. A failed cutover restores the entire code/config/source set and external preimages, then rebuilds and republishes the old contract; partial rollback or a dual reader is not allowed. No contract decision remains unresolved. RB-1.2 will require explicit writable access to the configured external-local source when that checkpoint is approved.

RB-1.0 review gate: the source syntax, descriptor, projection, runtime, workflow handling, host matrix, file/test shape, risks, and atomic rollback boundary are frozen. Do not begin RB-1.1 without explicit approval.

RB-1.1 — Add The Pure Report-Source Contract

  • [x] Add one shared report-source parser and normalized descriptor owner usable by builders and services without importing browser or management code.
  • [x] Validate zero-or-one cardinality, the closed attribute vocabulary, registered report/preset/context values, ignored Markdown contexts, exact source ranges, and actionable source-path errors.
  • [x] Reject mixed report front matter and block source through the new contract while leaving current product readers and current report-host documents unchanged until the atomic cutover.
  • [x] Add focused pure tests for valid declarations, optional context, malformed syntax, duplicates, unknown values, code/comment examples, and stable normalized output.

RB-1.1 evidence

  • Added docs-viewer/services/docs_report_source.py as the dependency-light shared owner. It exposes an immutable registry/host contract, immutable normalized descriptor, fixed payload projection, exact body range, and source-path-aware validation error. It imports only the standard library and the repository's pinned markdown-it-py parser; it does not import builder, management, browser, report-controller, or service workflow code.
  • Literal-context discovery reuses CommonMark tokens for fenced and indented code, inline code, HTML comments, and raw <pre>/<code> regions. The exact report token and its five closed attributes remain code-owned and fail closed outside those literal contexts.
  • Added docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_report_source.py: 41 focused cases pass across zero-or-one cardinality, exact syntax and isolation, optional context, registry validation, duplicates, retired front matter, unknown values, sub-scope rules, ignored contexts, immutable stable output, CRLF/line offsets, and source ranges/errors.
  • The final physical footprint is 349 production lines and 296 test lines. The production owner exceeds RB-1.0's rough line estimate while retaining the exact two-file shape; the user approved lightweight inserted-token validation, and the final version removes the draft's duplicate Markdown-context scanner in favor of the existing parser dependency.
  • Exact evidence passes: focused pytest (41 passed), changed-file bin/lint-python, py_compile, actual ten-report registry normalization and descriptor smoke, Studio docs dry build (304 documents, zero writes/removals/warnings), Studio search dry build (zero writes), generated JSON parsing, and git diff --check.
  • Deliberate omissions remain: no product import of the parser, no current viewer_report* reader or writer change, no report-host source migration, no generated report payload or markup change, and no browser/runtime integration.

Checkpoint: the pure parser and tests pass without changing current report rendering, projections, services, or source documents. Stop before RB-1.2 approval; the tracked product still uses the old contract at this intermediate review gate.

RB-1.2 — Perform The Atomic Product And Source Cutover

  • [x] Integrate the normalized descriptor into source records, Manage/public payload construction, exact inert-host rendering, and the existing report metadata validation path.
  • [x] Make public and Manage report composition mount into the generated host, preserve unavailable/error behavior, and release the exact current report through existing navigation and document-generation lifecycle.
  • [x] Move every direct service consumer and lifecycle-created host writer to the shared report-source owner; no service independently scans raw Markdown or retains a private report-field reader.
  • [x] Apply the RB-1.0 decisions to Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export workflows so body placement cannot bypass structural report validation.
  • [x] Convert every inventoried report-host source to one block, rebuild every affected working/public/search projection, and verify exact report id, access, scope, preset, sub-scope, document identity, and route behavior before and after migration.
  • [x] Remove the five active viewer_report* source fields, flat payload construction and browser normalization paths, lifecycle template fields, direct service readers, fixtures, and tests that assert the retired contract.
  • [x] Retain no dual reader, compatibility alias, precedence rule, migration mode, stale generated field, or unconverted active report host when the checkpoint completes.

RB-1.2 evidence

  • Source records and builders now parse through the shared owner, project one fixed-shape report object only in by-ID payloads, and replace the exact source range with the inert host. Public output retains public descriptors and hosts and removes local ones.
  • Manage and public controllers resolve exactly one generated host inside the current document content, never append a second root, and reject stale asynchronous work after navigation. Existing registries, executable loader allowlists, report implementations, data authorities, routes, and styles remain unchanged.
  • Direct Source, metadata, Publishability, Import, transfer, Review, rendered package, static HTML, document location, Publish, deletion, lifecycle creation, and Studio tag-document creation now preserve, validate, omit, or reject report structure according to the frozen RB-1.0 decisions. Inserted-token validation remains deliberately lightweight while the complete candidate is revalidated before write.
  • The 13 inventoried hosts were converted atomically: two Analysis public hosts, six Studio local hosts, and five external-local dotlineform hosts. A preimage assertion proves each edit contains only retired-front-matter removal plus the canonical appended block and preserves every prior timestamp and all other bytes. The 13 working and two public by-ID payloads each carry the exact descriptor and one host; 329 authoritative source documents and those payloads contain zero active retired fields.
  • The Analysis Works and dotlineform Projects lifecycle receipts were recomputed from the final source bytes. Studio, Analysis, and dotlineform docs and search were rebuilt; final dry builds report 304, 18, and 7 documents respectively with zero writes, removals, or warnings, all three search dry runs report zero writes, and Analysis Publish confirmation reports zero changed or excluded files.
  • Focused Python evidence passes across parser/builder/public projection, source and mutation services, location, Publish, lifecycle/deletion, transfer, Import, Review/package/static export, Catalogue follow-through, and Studio tag creation. Recorded groups are 178 passed; 50 passed; 44 passed; 31 passed with one skip; six focused workflow cases passed; and 18 Studio tag cases passed. Report-module, create/delete workflow, service-Manage, and Studio tag API smokes pass.
  • RB-1.2 review caught a Manage-startup regression: capabilities generation was sending all 634 configured source documents through CommonMark report-context parsing, including bodies with no report token. The shared parser now rejects retired front matter first and returns immediately when :::report is absent; possible, malformed, and literal-context declarations still take the complete parser path. The capability owner also no longer reads scope documents solely to emit an unused count. The live pre-fix endpoint measured 1.43 seconds, the parser fast path reduced that to 0.16–0.17 seconds, and the final source-independent handshake measures 0.053–0.059 seconds. The pending handshake is silent while management controls remain unavailable until the response resolves. The focused parser and capabilities group passes 52 tests, including proof that the no-token path does not call CommonMark and capabilities do not parse source documents.
  • Changed-file lint passes for 53 Python and six JavaScript files. Generated JSON parses, lifecycle hashes match exact source bytes, and git diff --check passes.

Checkpoint: all current reports mount at their exact block positions in the intended public or Manage context; all affected services resolve exact hosts through the normalized descriptor; migrated source and generated products contain no active retired fields; focused Python, JavaScript, builder, lifecycle, public-boundary, and report smokes pass. Stop before RB-1.3 closeout approval.

RB-1.3 — Verify And Transfer Durable Ownership

  • [ ] Run the bounded retired-contract scan over production code, active source documents, generated payloads, tests, and configuration, distinguishing deliberate historical documentation from active readers or writers.
  • [ ] Verify every configured report host and the complete public/local report registry-to-loader agreement, including lifecycle-created sub-scope hosts and external-local sources available to the delivery environment.
  • [ ] Run affected scope docs/search dry builds, focused source lint, changed Python/JavaScript lint, the warranted Docs Viewer smoke profile, generated assertions, and git diff --check.
  • [ ] Update Reports with the shipped block source contract, normalized payload and exact-position runtime; update durable sub-scope documentation with normalized host discovery; update Report Capability and Composition only if its durable module boundary actually changed.
  • [ ] Record exact implementation and verification evidence here, prepare the explicit feature/delivery closeout recommendation, and stop for user approval before changing status or retiring any document.

Checkpoint: durable documentation describes the shipped contract, focused and boundary evidence passes, and the closeout list is ready for explicit approval. RB-1 remains open until the user approves closeout.

Focused Evidence Contract

RB-1.0 chooses the smallest exact commands after the changed seams are known. Expected evidence includes:

  • pure parser/normalizer tests for grammar, cardinality, ignored contexts, attributes, registry validation, and normalized descriptors;
  • builder tests for exact placeholder position and projection-specific payload/HTML behavior;
  • service tests for sub-scope creation/discovery, document locations, publish gating, deletion, transfer, and each affected complete-source workflow;
  • JavaScript module tests or smokes proving public/Manage mounting into the existing host, unavailable behavior, navigation cleanup, and absence of a second appended root;
  • a full current-host migration assertion over authoritative sources and generated payloads;
  • focused bin/lint-python and bin/lint-js over changed source, affected scope docs/search builds, the warranted Docs Viewer smoke profile, and git diff --check.

Broad suites are warranted only when RB-1.0 finds a shared source or lifecycle owner whose risk cannot be proved through narrower tests. Browser checks are reserved for exact route/module/mount boundaries rather than ordinary layout or copy review.

Acceptance

RB-1 is complete only when:

  • every active report-host document has exactly one valid report block and no viewer_report* front matter;
  • every non-report document has no report block and emits no report descriptor or host;
  • invalid, duplicate, mixed, and unknown declarations fail with exact source evidence;
  • builders and services consume one normalized source owner, and browsers consume one normalized payload descriptor and exact inert host;
  • reports preserve current public/local availability, data sources, route state, lifecycle behavior, and immutable document host identity;
  • docs_subscope creation, public child reachability, location composition, deletion, transfer, and recorded lifecycle host behavior remain exact;
  • complete-source workflows cannot accidentally turn report configuration into unvalidated prose or executable browser configuration;
  • active source, production code, config, tests, and generated products contain no compatibility reader or stale field contract;
  • durable Reports and sub-scope documentation are current.

Durable Closeout

The primary shipped contract moves into Reports. Exact sub-scope report-host discovery remains in Sub-Scope Customisation Architecture, and Report Capability and Composition continues to own public/local module, data, contribution, and stylesheet separation.

At closeout, Report Blocks should be reviewed for retention as a concise feature rationale or retirement after its stable mental model has been transferred. RB-1 remains as delivery evidence until the user explicitly approves its closeout treatment. Catalogue Works Report Migration becomes eligible for its own sanity checkpoint only after RB-1 is accepted and closed.
